messages.author: 06fe2386ffb8b7dc
messages.subject: drawing lines between points in a dotplot
parts:
Hi folks,

I hope I am following the guidelines correctly.  This is my first post to this group.  I have tried to find a solution to my problem in the archives of this and other groups but cannot.

This is an example dataset:

newdf <- data.frame(ID=c("aa", "ab", "ac", "ad", "ae", "af", "aa", "ab", "ac", "ad", "ae", "af"),
                           Sex=rep(c("male", "female"), 6),
                           Group=c("old", "old","old","old","old","old","new","new","new","new","new","new"),
                           score=c(12:1))


(sorry my code isn't the most elegant)


I can then produce a dotplot using the following code:

ggplot(newdf, aes(x = factor(Sex), fill = factor(Group), y = score)) +
  geom_dotplot(binaxis = "y", stackdir = "center", position = "dodge") 


What I would like to do is draw a line between individual data points that belong to the same individual (ID).   i.e. I would like to connect the datapoints for groups "new" and "old" for each ID within the 'female' and within the 'male' factors.  I attach a sample figure that I mocked up (I manually put the lines in), that is the kind of thing I'm after.

My actual data I'm trying to do this with has many, many dots in the dotplot and some IDs go up and others go down.   I really like the dotplot for this presentation purpose, so would ideally have a solution using geom_dotplot



Many thanks

James Curley

messages.author: f4249b01b99d0091
messages.subject: Re: drawing lines between points in a dotplot
parts:
This is a bit of a hack, but see what you think of this:

library( reshape )
newdf1 <- cast(newdf,ID+Sex~Group)
ggplot(newdf1)+geom_point(aes(x=paste(Sex,"new"),y=new),color='red',size=5)+geom_point(aes(x=paste(Sex,"old"),y=old),color='blue',size=5)+geom_segment(aes(x=paste(Sex,"new"),xend=paste(Sex,"old"),y=new,yend=old))

Ben

messages.subject: Re: drawing lines between points in a dotplot
parts:
Thanks Ben,

That does work ok.

I have come up with a kind of solution to my original question using
faceting, whilst still using the geom_dotplot:

p<-ggplot(newdf, aes(x=Group, y=score))+
geom_path(aes(color = Sex, group = factor(ID)))+
geom_dotplot(binaxis="y", binwidth = .5,stackdir = "centerwhole")
p + facet_grid(. ~ Sex)

If possible, I still would like to get it into one chart without faceting


thanks for your help
James Curley

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: drawing lines between points in a dotplot
parts:
Hi:

I like the plot you generated, since it's visually less cluttered and
you can still compare male-female differences side-by-side.

You can, however, put the two of them together by removing
facet_grid(). With a couple of cosmetic changes:

newdf <- data.frame(ID = c("aa", "ab", "ac", "ad", "ae", "af"),

Group = rep(c("old", "new"), each = 6),
score = 12:1)

ggplot(newdf, aes(x=Group, y=score)) +
geom_path(aes(color = Sex, group = ID), size = 1) +
geom_dotplot(aes(fill = Sex), binaxis="y", binwidth = .5,stackdir =
"centerwhole") +
scale_color_manual(values = c("orange", "blue")) +
scale_fill_manual(values = c("orange", "blue"))

The last two lines give you control over the rendered colors.

Dennis
